fullPassage:
"Good things come in small packages," they say. Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate the importance of small things, often putting them together to create amazing works of art. Often, practical need or creative desire plays a key role in such efforts.
Patchwork, whose beauty has long been appreciated in many cultures across the globe, is a type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric together to create a larger piece of art. Every culture is proud of its own patterns, including Koreans, who take pride in their unique style, jogakbo. Created during the Joseon dynasty, it is a type of traditional wrapping cloth made by stitching small pieces of fabric into a large square or rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste any fabric and found ways to reuse it. However, jogakbo was much more than just repurposing fabric. It often told the creator's life story because a finished piece contained fabric scraps from her wedding skirt, her husband's shirt, and her children's clothes. The practical need to repurpose leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.
The beauty of jogakbo lies in its design, which results from stitching together patches of various shapes, sizes, and colors in a seemingly improvised manner. Stitching such random patches into a perfect square or rectangle requires artistic sensitivity, a high level of skill, careful planning, and long hours stitching. The desire for creative excellence resulted in harmonious combinations of patches in various colors, shapes, and sizes, which have been compared to modern abstract paintings, such as those of Piet Mondrian or Paul Klee. Jogakbo was a useful activity in which leftover pieces of cloth were transformed into a pursuit of beauty and utility, eventually becoming an important part of traditional Korean craft art.
The Sainte-Chapelle in Paris, France and Nasir al-Mulk mosque in Shiraz, Iran amaze their visitors with brilliant glass window panels through which astonishing light of vigorous colors penetrates. These panels are called stained-glass windows and are made up of colored pieces of glass assembled together to form large windows. In Europe and the Middle East, the techniques for stained-glass windows advanced quickly during the Medieval period, when religious buildings got bigger to accommodate more worshipers and prayers. Small pieces of glass assembled next to one another were not only more practical for construction but also able to tell a story. Since most people were illiterate at that time, the images placed on the windows helped them understand religious messages that they might otherwise have been unable to grasp.
Making a stained-glass window is a process in which intricacy is required. It involves creating durable glass sheets and staining them, cutting them into desired shapes, and assembling them into prepared designs. Each step requires expert craftspeople working together. Though originally used in religious structures, stained-glass windows found their way into a variety of modern buildings, including residential homes. These little pieces are now recognized worldwide as an important form of creative art, whose splendor wouldn't have been acknowledged without the glass artists' desire for beauty sparked by a practical need.
Throughout the ages and across all cultures, there have been small decorative objects with a hole for threading called beads. In its simplest form, beadwork can involve threading a few beads together on a single string to make a simple bracelet or necklace, or on a larger scale, to form beaded bags, clothing, or even wall-hangings. Beadwork is ancient, evidenced by the findings of beads dating back to the Stone Age. Back then, people strung bones, shells, or rocks together to hang around their neck. As cultures and societies evolved over time, beadwork became a form of personal expression, a symbol of social class, or even a talisman to drive away bad luck.
Interestingly, some regions have particularly rich traditions. The Ndebele tribe of South Africa, for example, is famed for intricate dresses made of glass beads. Different designs serve as a means of marking different developmental stages of a woman's life. An unmarried girl may wear a square apron onto which thousands of glass beads were hand-sewn, while a married woman might wear a five-paneled apron, along with beaded necklaces and a beaded cape. Similarly, beadwork is an essential aspect of many Native American cultures. Beadwork powerfully expresses cultural identity, reflecting a sense of continuity across generations.
Plato once remarked that "our need will be the real creator." When need or desire arises, different communities willingly attach small, simple, insignificant everyday objects to one another to generate a new form of creative work that is more beautiful and more practical than the mere sum of its parts. The Greek philosopher may have recognized that the process for all things creative begins from within, from need and desire, to express artistic instincts or to maximize the utility of things available. Cultures may vary on the surface, but they all seem to share some common elements, often universal and essential, rooted deep in human nature.

questions.passage: Patchwork, whose beauty has long been appreciated in many cultures across the globe, is a type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric together to create a larger piece of art. Every culture is proud of its own patterns, including Koreans, who take pride in their unique style, jogakbo. Created during the Joseon dynasty, it is a type of traditional wrapping cloth made by stitching small pieces of fabric into a large square or rectangle. (A)[Frugal / Extravagant] women did not want to waste any fabric and found ways to (B)[reuse / discard] it. However, jogakbo was much more than just (C)[repurposing / abandoning] fabric.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 검소한(Frugal) 여인들은 조금의 천도 낭비하기를 원하지 않았고 그것을 재사용(reuse)하는 방법을 찾아냈다. 조각보는 단순히 천을 재활용(repurposing)하는 것 이상의 의미를 지녔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Frugal–reuse–repurposing: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ① Extravagant(사치스러운)은 '낭비를 원하지 않았다'는 문맥과 모순
❌ ③ discard(버리다)는 reuse(재사용하다)의 반의어
❌ ④ Extravagant+discard 조합은 문맥과 완전히 반대
det.tip: Frugal(검소한) ↔ Extravagant(사치스러운) / reuse(재사용하다) ↔ discard(버리다) / repurpose(재활용하다) ↔ abandon(포기하다)

det.analysis:

det.tip: improvised(즉흥적인) ≈ spontaneous ↔ planned(계획된), deliberate(의도적인)

questions.passage: "Good things come in small packages," they say. Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate the importance of small things, often putting them together to create amazing works of art. Often, <u>practical</u> need or creative desire plays a key role in such efforts. Patchwork is a type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric together to create a larger piece of art.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 practical과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 실용적인(practical) 필요성이나 창작 욕구가 중요한 역할을 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① theoretical(이론적인): practical(실용적인)의 정반대
❌ ② useful(유용한): practical과 비슷한 의미 (동의어)
❌ ③ functional(기능적인): practical과 비슷한 의미
❌ ④ realistic(현실적인): practical과 유사한 의미
det.tip: practical(실용적인) ↔ theoretical(이론적인), impractical(비실용적인) / practical ≈ useful, functional

questions.passage:
(A) The practical need to repurpose leftover patches gave birth to a novel art <u>form</u>. The beauty of jogakbo lies in its design, which results from stitching together patches of various shapes, sizes, and colors.

(B) These panels are called stained-glass windows and are made up of colored pieces of glass assembled together to <u>form</u> large windows. In Europe and the Middle East, the techniques for stained-glass windows advanced quickly during the Medieval period.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 form의 의미로 알맞은 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 새로운 예술 형태(form)를 탄생시켰다. (B) 큰 창을 형성하기(form) 위해 짜맞추어졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 형태–형성하다: (A)에서 form은 명사로 '형태', (B)에서 form은 동사로 '형성하다'
❌ ① 양식–형성하다: (A)의 art form은 '예술 양식'보다 '예술 형태'가 더 적합
❌ ② 형태–구성하다: (B)에서 'to form windows'는 '구성하다'보다 '형성하다'가 적합
❌ ④ 양식–구성하다: (A)(B) 모두 부적합
det.tip: form — 명사: 형태, 형식, 양식 / 동사: 형성하다, 만들다 / 문맥에 따라 품사+의미 판단

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어는?
"careful about spending money or using things, not wanting to waste anything"

det.korean: 돈을 쓰거나 물건을 사용하는 데 조심스러운, 아무것도 낭비하기를 원하지 않는 → 검소한(frugal)
det.analysis:
✅ ① frugal(검소한): 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ② generous(관대한): frugal의 반의어, 베풀기 좋아하는
❌ ③ practical(실용적인): 돈 사용보다 기능적 측면
❌ ④ creative(창의적인): 절약과 무관
det.tip: frugal(검소한) ≈ thrifty, economical ↔ generous(관대한), wasteful(낭비하는)

questions.passage: Each culture has its own distinct patterns of patchwork. This craft has long been __________ (appreciate) in many cultures across the globe for its beauty and creativity.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 공예는 오래도록 많은 문화권에서 그 아름다움과 창의성으로 인정받아(appreciated) 왔다.
det.analysis: has been + 과거분사(p.p.) 형태: 현재완료 수동태. appreciate → appreciated
det.tip: have/has been + p.p. = 현재완료 수동태 (~되어 왔다) / appreciate(감상하다, 인정하다)

questions.passage: These small pieces are now __________ (recognize) worldwide as an important form of creative art. Their beauty would not have been possible without the artists' desire.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 작은 조각들은 이제 세계적으로 중요한 창의적 예술의 형태로 인정받고(recognized) 있다.
det.analysis:
are now + 과거분사(p.p.) 형태: 현재 수동태. recognize → recognized
'worldwide'와 'as an important form'이 수동 의미를 보강
det.tip: be + p.p. = 수동태 / recognize(인정하다, 알아보다) → recognized(인정받는)

questions.passage: Patchwork, whose beauty has long been appreciated in many cultures across the globe, is a type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric together to create a larger piece of art. Every culture is proud of its own patterns, including Koreans, who take pride in their unique style, jogakbo. Created during the Joseon dynasty, it is a type of traditional wrapping cloth made by stitching small pieces of fabric into a large square or rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste any fabric and found ways to reuse it. However, jogakbo was much more than just repurposing fabric. The practical need to repurpose leftover patches __________ a novel art form.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 남은 조각을 재활용하기 위한 실용적인 필요성이 새로운 예술 형태를 탄생시켰다(gave birth to).
det.analysis:
✅ ② gave birth to(~을 탄생시키다): 실용적 필요가 새 예술 형태를 만들어냈다는 긍정적 인과관계
❌ ① put an end to(~을 끝내다): 새 예술 형태가 탄생했으므로 반대 의미
❌ ③ took away from(~에서 빼앗다): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ stood in the way of(~을 방해하다): 탄생이 아니라 방해의 의미
det.tip: give birth to = ~을 탄생시키다, ~을 낳다 / put an end to = ~을 끝내다 / stand in the way of = ~을 방해하다

questions.passage: Making a stained-glass window is a process in which intricacy is required. It involves creating durable glass sheets and staining them, cutting them into desired shapes, and assembling them into prepared designs. Each step requires expert craftspeople working together. Though originally used in religious structures, stained-glass windows __________ a variety of modern buildings, including residential homes. These little pieces are now recognized worldwide as an important form of creative art.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 스테인드글라스 창은 본래 종교 건물에서 사용되었으나 다양한 현대 건물 속으로 들어갔다(found their way into).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ found their way into(~에 진출하다): 종교 건물→현대 건물로 확산되었다는 의미
❌ ① kept away from(~에서 멀리하다): 현대 건물에 사용된다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② were removed from(~에서 제거되다): 확산이 아니라 제거의 의미
❌ ④ were excluded from(~에서 배제되다): 확산과 반대 의미
det.tip: find one's way into = ~에 들어가다, ~에 진출하다 (관용 표현) / Though originally used in A, S found their way into B = 원래 A에서 사용되었지만 B로 확산되었다
